```python
        return NULL if v is None else round(float(v), n)
    feats = []
    for i, r in enumerate(result["rows"]):
        f = QgsFeature(pl.fields())
        f.setGeometry(QgsGeometry.fromPointXY(QgsPointXY(r["x"], r["y"])))
        arr = r.get("arrival")
        note = r.get("extra") or ""
        if arr is None and r.get("arrival_channel") is not None:
            note = (note + "; " if note else "") + "channel arrival {} h:min".format(
                hhmm(r["arrival_channel"]))
        f.setAttributes([i + 1, round(r["rm"], 2), r["kind"], r["name"] or NULL,
                         round(r["offset_ft"], 0), nz(arr), hhmm(arr) or NULL,
                         nz(r.get("depth")), nz(r.get("peak")),
                         NULL if r.get("n_struct") is None else int(r["n_struct"]),
                         note or NULL])
        feats.append(f)
    pl.dataProvider().addFeatures(feats)
    pl.updateExtents()
    ll = create_memory_layer("EAP_Channel_Centerline", WKB_LINESTRING, crs,
                             [QgsField("Source", FT_STRING), QgsField("Length_mi", FT_DOUBLE)])
    f = QgsFeature(ll.fields())
    f.setGeometry(QgsGeometry.fromPolylineXY([QgsPointXY(x, y) for x, y in result["line"]]))
    f.setAttributes([result.get("source") or "", NULL])
    ll.dataProvider().addFeatures([f])
    ll.updateExtents()
    return pl, ll


def summary_lines(result, layer_name="EAP_Travel_Time"):
    rows = result.get("rows") or []
    st = [r for r in rows if r["kind"] == "Station"]
    out = []
    if not st:
        return ["Travel-time table not made: " + "; ".join(result.get("notes") or [
            "no centerline"])]
    wet = [r for r in st if r.get("depth") is not None]
    out.append("{} stations along {:.1f} river miles ({}); flood on the channel to river "
               "mile {:.1f} - EAP/{}.csv / .xlsx".format(
                   len(st), st[-1]["rm"], result.get("source") or "centerline",
                   wet[-1]["rm"] if wet else 0.0, layer_name))
    key = [r for r in rows if r["kind"] in ("Town", "Bridge / crossing", "Dam")]
    key.sort(key=lambda r: r["rm"])
    if key:
        out.append("First arrival: " + "; ".join(
            "{} RM {:.1f} {}".format(r["name"], r["rm"], hhmm(
                r.get("arrival") if r.get("arrival") is not None else
                r.get("arrival_channel")) or "-") for r in key[:8]) +
            ("" if len(key) <= 8 else " and {} more".format(len(key) - 8)))
    for n in result.get("notes") or []:
        out.append("Note: " + n)
    return out
```

## `watch.py`

```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Hazard-creep watch: re-classify every dam of a folder against fresh data
(NSI, address points, building outlines, roads ...) and report what changed
since each dam's previous run.

A hazard classification is only as current as the data behind it: houses
built below a dam, a new subdivision, a re-routed road or a changed NSI
population can move a dam into a higher class years after the last study
(hazard creep). The watch re-runs each dam with the SAME flood rasters but
new downloads, compares the result with the dam's previous run (the same
comparison as QA/Changes_Since_Last_Run.csv) and lists, per dam, whether the
class changed and what caused it. Dams with an alert come first.

It can run from the Processing toolbox / the Hazard Classification tab, or on
a schedule with qgis_process (see the README). It never changes a dam's
classification decision - it produces the list of dams to look at.

Two run modes (v2.8; v2.9: shared with the batch classification):
  sequential  every dam is classified one after another in this QGIS session
              (processing_provider.batch_classify) - the default, and what runs
              when nothing else is possible;
  parallel    `workers` > 1: every dam is a separate `qgis_process run
              ndhazard:classify` child process, at most `workers` at a time. A
              child works on its own dam folder only and writes the same files
              as a sequential run (outputs/QA/Last_Run_Snapshot.json,
              Changes_Since_Last_Run.csv ...); the watch reads its rows from
              those files, never from the child's text output. The fresh-data
              settings travel in a small JSON file (CONFIG_JSON parameter of
              the classify algorithm, see processing_provider.py) and the
              offline data pack choice in environment variables. A per-dam
              timeout ends a stuck child; a failed or timed-out dam is a FAILED
              row with the tail of the child's error output; Cancel terminates
              all children. When qgis_process cannot be found (or this is no
              real QGIS) the watch falls back to the sequential mode and says
              so in the log and in the report.

v2.9: the watch IS a batch classification (processing_provider.batch_classify,
in either mode) followed by the comparison of each dam's snapshots, so both
modes also write Batch_Hazard_Classification.csv. The worker machinery below
(plan_mode, run_workers, find_qgis_process ...) is used by both. A dam whose
run finished without writing a NEW Last_Run_Snapshot.json is a FAILED row
("not compared"), never "no change" read from the old snapshot.
"""

import csv
import html
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time

from . import history as HIS
from .constants import OUTPUT_FOLDER_NAME, SUBDIR_QA, PLUGIN_NAME, PLUGIN_VERSION

WATCH_FIELDS = ["Alert", "Dam", "Status", "ND_Before", "ND_Now", "TM11_Before", "TM11_Now",
                "LIJ_Before", "LIJ_Now", "Flooded_Habitable_Before", "Flooded_Habitable_Now",
                "Newly_Flooded", "No_Longer_Flooded", "Category_Changes", "Roads_Newly_Overtopped",
                "Lifelines_Newly_Inundated", "Compared_With", "Message", "Folder"]
CSV_LATEST = "Hazard_Creep_Watch.csv"
_ND_RANK = {"Low": 1, "Medium": 2, "High": 3}
_DRY = ("", None, "Not inundated")

ALERT_CLASS_UP = "CLASS UP"
ALERT_CLASS_CHANGE = "CLASS CHANGE"
ALERT_CREEP = "CREEP"
ALERT_REVIEW = "REVIEW"
ALERT_NEW = "BASELINE"
ALERT_NONE = "-"
ALERT_FAILED = "FAILED"
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 3600            # per dam, parallel mode (0 = no limit)
MAX_WORKERS = 16
ENV_QGIS_PROCESS = "ND_QGIS_PROCESS"    # full path of qgis_process (or its .bat wrapper)
WATCH_WORKER_LOG = "Watch_Worker_Log.txt"   # <dam>/outputs: a failed worker's full output
BATCH_WORKER_LOG = "Batch_Worker_Log.txt"
_POLL_S = 0.25
_TAIL_LINES = 6
_TAIL_CHARS = 600
_KILL_GRACE_S = 5.0
_sleep = time.sleep                 # module level so tests can replace them
_clock = time.monotonic
_ALERT_ORDER = [ALERT_FAILED, ALERT_CLASS_UP, ALERT_CLASS_CHANGE, ALERT_CREEP, ALERT_REVIEW,
                ALERT_NEW, ALERT_NONE]

# what the change rows (history.diff) are called
_NEW, _GONE = "Newly flooded / cut off", "No longer flooded / cut off"
_CAT = ("Structure category", "Habitable")


def dam_folders(parent):
    """The dam folders directly inside `parent` (as the batch classification
    lists them)."""
    return sorted(os.path.join(parent, d) for d in os.listdir(parent)
                  if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(parent, d)) and not d.startswith(("_", "."))
                  and d.lower() != OUTPUT_FOLDER_NAME)


def qa_folder(dam_folder):
    return os.path.join(dam_folder, OUTPUT_FOLDER_NAME, SUBDIR_QA)


def snapshot_path(dam_folder):
    return os.path.join(qa_folder(dam_folder), HIS.SNAPSHOT_FILE)


def file_mark(path):
    """What identifies this version of a file (None: no file). A run that
    rewrites the file changes it: history.write_snapshot replaces the file
    (new inode / file id and time) - no clock comparison, so a network
    drive with another clock cannot make an old file look new."""
    try:
        st = os.stat(path)
    except OSError:
        return None
    return (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size, st.st_ino, getattr(st, "st_ctime_ns", 0))


def read_before(dam_folder):
    """The dam's last-run snapshot (before the watch re-runs it), or None."""
    return HIS.read_snapshot(qa_folder(dam_folder))


def read_changes(dam_folder):
    """Change rows [(Change, Item, Before, Now)] of the run just made."""
    path = os.path.join(qa_folder(dam_folder), HIS.CHANGES_FILE)
    try:
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            return [(r.get("Change", ""), r.get("Item", ""), r.get("Before", ""),
                     r.get("Now", "")) for r in csv.DictReader(fh)]
    except OSError:
        return []


def flooded_habitable(snap):
    return sum(1 for s in (snap or {}).get("structures", [])
               if s.get("habitable") == "Yes" and s.get("outcome") not in _DRY)


def summarise(name, folder, before, after, changes=()):
    """One watch row from the dam's snapshots before / after the re-run and
    the change rows of that run. Pure data: testable without QGIS."""
    row = dict.fromkeys(WATCH_FIELDS, "")
    row.update({"Dam": name, "Folder": folder, "Alert": ALERT_NONE, "Status": "done",
                "ND_Now": (after or {}).get("nd") or "", "TM11_Now": (after or {}).get("tm11")
                or "", "LIJ_Now": (after or {}).get("lij", ""),
                "Flooded_Habitable_Now": flooded_habitable(after)})
    if before is None:
        row.update({"Alert": ALERT_NEW, "Message": "no earlier run to compare with - this run "
                    "is the baseline for the next watch"})
        return row
    row.update({"ND_Before": before.get("nd") or "", "TM11_Before": before.get("tm11") or "",
                "LIJ_Before": before.get("lij", ""), "Compared_With": before.get("time") or "",
                "Flooded_Habitable_Before": flooded_habitable(before)})
    n_new = sum(1 for c in changes if c[0] == _NEW)
    n_gone = sum(1 for c in changes if c[0] == _GONE)
    n_cat = sum(1 for c in changes if c[0] in _CAT)
    n_road = sum(1 for c in changes if c[0] == "Road newly overtopped")
    n_life = sum(1 for c in changes if c[0] == "Lifeline newly inundated")
    row.update({"Newly_Flooded": n_new, "No_Longer_Flooded": n_gone, "Category_Changes": n_cat,
                "Roads_Newly_Overtopped": n_road, "Lifelines_Newly_Inundated": n_life})
    nd_b, nd_a = before.get("nd"), (after or {}).get("nd")
    tm_b, tm_a = before.get("tm11"), (after or {}).get("tm11")
    why = []
    if nd_b != nd_a or tm_b != tm_a:
        up = _ND_RANK.get(nd_a, 0) > _ND_RANK.get(nd_b, 0) or \
            _ND_RANK.get(tm_a, 0) > _ND_RANK.get(tm_b, 0)
        if nd_b != nd_a:
            why.append("ND {} -> {}".format(nd_b, nd_a))
        if tm_b != tm_a:
            why.append("TM 11 {} -> {}".format(tm_b, tm_a))
        row["Alert"] = ALERT_CLASS_UP if up else ALERT_CLASS_CHANGE
    elif n_new or n_life or n_road or _lij_up(before, after):
        row["Alert"] = ALERT_CREEP
    elif n_gone or n_cat:
        row["Alert"] = ALERT_REVIEW
    if n_new:
        why.append("{} structure(s) newly flooded or cut off".format(n_new))
    if n_life:
        why.append("{} lifeline / critical facilit(ies) newly inundated".format(n_life))
    if n_road:
        why.append("{} road stretch(es) newly overtopped".format(n_road))
    if _lij_up(before, after):
        why.append("lives in jeopardy {} -> {}".format(before.get("lij"), after.get("lij")))
    if n_gone:
        why.append("{} structure(s) no longer flooded".format(n_gone))
    if n_cat:
        why.append("{} structure(s) with another habitability / category".format(n_cat))
    row["Message"] = "; ".join(why) or "no change"
    return row


def _lij_up(before, after):
    try:
        return float(after.get("lij")) > float(before.get("lij")) + 0.05
    except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        return False


def failed_row(name, folder, status, message):
    row = dict.fromkeys(WATCH_FIELDS, "")
    row.update({"Dam": name, "Folder": folder, "Status": status, "Message": message,
                "Alert": ALERT_FAILED if status == "failed" else ALERT_NONE})
    return row


def sort_rows(rows):
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (_ALERT_ORDER.index(r["Alert"]) if r["Alert"]
                                       in _ALERT_ORDER else 99, str(r["Dam"]).lower()))


def counts(rows):
    return {a: sum(1 for r in rows if r["Alert"] == a) for a in _ALERT_ORDER}


def alerts_text(rows):
    """One line: how many dams need a look."""
    c = counts(rows)
    hot = c[ALERT_CLASS_UP] + c[ALERT_CLASS_CHANGE] + c[ALERT_CREEP] + c[ALERT_REVIEW]
    return ("{} dam(s) watched: {} class change(s) ({} up), {} with creep, {} to review, {} "
            "unchanged or baseline, {} failed".format(
                len(rows), c[ALERT_CLASS_UP] + c[ALERT_CLASS_CHANGE], c[ALERT_CLASS_UP],
                c[ALERT_CREEP], c[ALERT_REVIEW], len(rows) - hot - c[ALERT_FAILED],
                c[ALERT_FAILED]))


def write_reports(parent, rows, when=None, mode=None):
    """Hazard_Creep_Watch.csv (latest), Hazard_Creep_Watch_<date>.csv and
    .html (a table, alerts first) in `parent`. Returns {"csv", "dated", "html"}.
    `mode` (text, see mode_text) is named in the HTML header; the CSV columns
    are the same in every mode."""
    from .helpers import prepare_output_path
    when = when or time.localtime()
    day = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", when)
    rows = sort_rows(rows)
    paths = {}
    for key, name in (("csv", CSV_LATEST),
                      ("dated", "Hazard_Creep_Watch_{}.csv".format(day))):
        path = prepare_output_path(os.path.join(parent, name))
        with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=WATCH_FIELDS)
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(rows)
        paths[key] = path
    hpath = prepare_output_path(os.path.join(parent, "Hazard_Creep_Watch_{}.html".format(day)))
    with open(hpath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(_html(rows, day, mode))
    paths["html"] = hpath
    return paths


_COLOR = {ALERT_FAILED: "#b71c1c", ALERT_CLASS_UP: "#b71c1c", ALERT_CLASS_CHANGE: "#e65100",
          ALERT_CREEP: "#f9a825", ALERT_REVIEW: "#fdd835", ALERT_NEW: "#90caf9"}


def _html(rows, day, mode=None):
    cols = ["Alert", "Dam", "ND_Before", "ND_Now", "TM11_Before", "TM11_Now", "Newly_Flooded",
            "Compared_With", "Message"]
    out = ["<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset='utf-8'><title>Hazard creep watch {}"
           "</title><style>body{{font-family:sans-serif;margin:16px}}table{{border-collapse:"
           "collapse}}td,th{{border:1px solid #bbb;padding:3px 8px;font-size:13px}}th{{"
           "background:#eee}}</style></head><body>".format(html.escape(day)),
           "<h2>Hazard creep watch - {}</h2>".format(html.escape(day)),
           "<p>{}</p>".format(html.escape(alerts_text(rows)))]
    if mode:
        out.append("<p>Run mode: {}</p>".format(html.escape(mode)))
    out += [
           "<p>Each dam was re-classified with its own flood rasters and fresh data and "
           "compared with its previous run. This is a list of dams to look at, not a "
           "classification decision. {} v{}.</p>".format(html.escape(PLUGIN_NAME),
                                                        html.escape(PLUGIN_VERSION)),
           "<table><tr>" + "".join("<th>{}</th>".format(html.escape(c)) for c in cols)
           + "</tr>"]
    for r in rows:
        style = " style='background:{}'".format(_COLOR[r["Alert"]]) if r["Alert"] in _COLOR \
            else ""
        out.append("<tr>" + "".join(
            "<td{}>{}</td>".format(style if c == "Alert" else "", html.escape(str(r.get(c, ""))))
            for c in cols) + "</tr>")
    out.append("</table></body></html>")
    return "\n".join(out)


def fresh_data_config(cfg_over=None):
    """Settings for a watch run: the flood rasters are the dam's own but
    nothing of the downloads / inventory is re-used, the comparison with the
    previous run is on, nothing is added to a project."""
    # save_evaluation off: a folder of dams would fill the disk with caches
    # v2.8: downloads come from the per-tile cache when a tile is younger than
    # data_max_age_days (7): only tiles older than that are fetched again
    over = {"reuse_evaluation": False, "save_evaluation": False, "compare_last_run": True,
            "add_to_project": False, "report_pdf": False, "eap": False,
            "data_cache_folder": "auto", "data_max_age_days": 7}
    over.update(cfg_over or {})
    over.update({"reuse_evaluation": False, "compare_last_run": True,
                 "add_to_project": False})
    return over


# ------------------------------------------------------- worker processes --
class WorkerUnavailable(Exception):
    """The first worker process could not be started (no permission, broken
    install ...): the watch / batch falls back to the sequential mode."""


def default_workers():
    """Suggested number of parallel workers: min(3, CPU count)."""
    return max(1, min(3, os.cpu_count() or 1))


def _real_qgis():
    """True in a real QGIS (the test harness' fake QGIS has no prefixPath)."""
    try:
        from qgis.core import QgsApplication
        return callable(getattr(QgsApplication, "prefixPath", None))
    except Exception:
        return False


def _qgis_process_names():
    if os.name == "nt":
        return ["qgis_process-qgis-ltr.bat", "qgis_process-qgis.bat", "qgis_process.bat",
                "qgis_process.exe"]
    return ["qgis_process"]


def _is_exe(path):
    return bool(path) and os.path.isfile(path) and os.access(path, os.X_OK)


def find_qgis_process():
    """(path, note): the qgis_process executable of this QGIS installation, or
    (None, why not). Looked for, in this order: the environment variable
    ND_QGIS_PROCESS (a full path); the QGIS install directory (QgsApplication.
    prefixPath() / pkgDataPath(): <prefix>/bin, <prefix>, and on Windows the
    OSGeo4W wrapper qgis_process-qgis[-ltr].bat two levels above apps/qgis);
    the folder of the running QGIS program; PATH. Never raises."""
    if not _real_qgis():
        return None, "this is not a real QGIS session"
    note = ""
    env = os.environ.get(ENV_QGIS_PROCESS, "").strip().strip('"')
    if env:
        if _is_exe(env):
            return env, ""
        note = "{} points to {} which is not an executable file; ".format(ENV_QGIS_PROCESS, env)
    dirs = []
    try:
        from qgis.core import QgsApplication
        for base in (QgsApplication.prefixPath(), os.path.join(
                QgsApplication.pkgDataPath(), os.pardir, os.pardir)):
            if not base:
                continue
            base = os.path.normpath(str(base))
            dirs += [os.path.join(base, "bin"), base,
                     os.path.join(base, os.pardir, os.pardir, "bin")]
    except Exception:
        pass
    exe_dir = os.path.dirname(sys.executable or "")
    if exe_dir and "qgis" in os.path.basename(sys.executable or "").lower():
        dirs.append(exe_dir)
    for d in dirs:
        for name in _qgis_process_names():
            path = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(d, name))
            if _is_exe(path):
                return path, ""
    for name in _qgis_process_names():
        path = shutil.which(name)
        if path:
            return path, ""
    return None, note + "qgis_process was not found (set {} to its full path)".format(
        ENV_QGIS_PROCESS)


def worker_command(exe, dam_folder, settings_path):
    """The command line of one dam's worker: the Processing algorithm
    ndhazard:classify with the dam folder and the JSON settings file."""
    from .processing_provider import PROVIDER_ID
    return [exe, "run", PROVIDER_ID + ":classify", "--DAM_FOLDER=" + dam_folder,
            "--CONFIG_JSON=" + settings_path]


def worker_env(base=None):
    """Environment of the workers: the offline data pack choice of this
    session (a worker may use another QGIS profile), unbuffered output."""
    env = dict(os.environ if base is None else base)
    try:
        from .download import offline_config, ENV_PACK, ENV_ONLY
        path, only = offline_config()
        env[ENV_PACK] = path or ""
        env[ENV_ONLY] = "1" if only else "0"
    except Exception:
        pass
    env.setdefault("PYTHONUNBUFFERED", "1")
    return env


def _tail(path, lines=_TAIL_LINES, chars=_TAIL_CHARS):
    """Last lines of a text file on one line ('' when unreadable)."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            fh.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
            fh.seek(max(0, fh.tell() - 8192))
            text = fh.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    except OSError:
        return ""
    got = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()][-lines:]
    out = " | ".join(got)
    return out[-chars:] if len(out) > chars else out


def _terminate(proc, grace=None):
    """End a worker and whatever it started (the OSGeo4W .bat wrapper starts
    the real program as a child): terminate, then kill after `grace` s."""
    import subprocess
    grace = _KILL_GRACE_S if grace is None else grace
    real = type(proc).__module__ == "subprocess"        # never signal a test double's pid
    try:
        if real and os.name == "nt":
            subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(proc.pid), "/T", "/F"],
                           stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=15)
        elif real:
            import signal
            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGTERM)     # started in its own session
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        proc.terminate()
    except Exception:
        pass
    t0 = _clock()
    while proc.poll() is None and _clock() - t0 < grace:
        _sleep(0.05)
    if proc.poll() is None:
        try:
            if real and os.name != "nt":
                import signal
                os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            proc.kill()
        except Exception:
            pass


def _write_worker_log(folder, out_path, err_path, why, name=WATCH_WORKER_LOG,
                      what="hazard creep watch"):
    """Keep a failed worker's full output next to the dam's results."""
    try:
        target = os.path.join(folder, OUTPUT_FOLDER_NAME, name)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
        with open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write("{} - {} worker: {}\n\n".format(PLUGIN_NAME, what, why))
            for label, path in (("standard output", out_path), ("error output", err_path)):
                fh.write("=== {} ===\n".format(label))
                try:
                    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as src:
                        fh.write(src.read())
                except OSError:
                    pass
                fh.write("\n")
        return target
    except OSError:
        return ""


def run_workers(jobs, exe, workers, timeout_s=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S, work_dir=None, progress=None,
                log=None, popen=None, env=None, log_name=WATCH_WORKER_LOG,
                what="hazard creep watch"):
    """Run `jobs` [{"name", "folder", "settings"[, "result_path"]}] as
    qgis_process children, at most `workers` at a time, and wait for all of
    them. Returns {folder: (ok, message)}: ok when the child exited with 0;
    otherwise the message says why (exit code, timeout, could not start) with
    the tail of its error output (the full output goes to <dam>/outputs/
    `log_name`). A job's "result_path" is handed to the child in its settings
    file (processing_provider.RESULT_KEY): the classify algorithm writes its
    result there. Cancel (CancelledByUser from `progress`) or any other
    exception terminates every child still running before it propagates.
    Raises WorkerUnavailable when not a single worker could be started.
    `popen` replaces subprocess.Popen (tests)."""
    import subprocess
    from .processing_provider import write_worker_settings, RESULT_KEY
    popen = popen or subprocess.Popen
    work_dir = work_dir or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="nd_watch_")
    env = env if env is not None else worker_env()
    workers = max(1, int(workers))
    pending, running, results = list(jobs), [], {}
    total, finished, started_any = len(jobs), 0, False
    kw = {"start_new_session": True} if os.name != "nt" else {
        "creationflags": getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0x08000000)}

    def say(msg=None):
        if progress is None:
            return
        names = ", ".join(j["name"] for j in running)
        progress(100.0 * finished / max(1, total),
                 msg or "{}/{} dam(s) finished{}".format(
                     finished, total, "; running: " + names if names else ""))

    def close(job):
        for fh in (job.get("out"), job.get("err")):
            try:
                fh.close()
            except Exception:
                pass

    def end(job, ok, message):
        nonlocal finished
        close(job)
        running.remove(job)
        finished += 1
        results[job["folder"]] = (ok, message)
        secs = _clock() - job["t0"]
        if ok:
            note = "done in {:.0f} s".format(secs)
        else:
            note = "FAILED - " + message
            logfile = _write_worker_log(job["folder"], job["out_path"], job["err_path"],
                                        message, log_name, what)
            if logfile:
                note += " (full worker output: {})".format(logfile)
        if log:
            log("{} ({}/{}): {}".format(job["name"], finished, total, note))

    try:
        while pending or running:
            while pending and len(running) < workers:
                job = dict(pending.pop(0))
                idx = len(results) + len(running) + 1
                stem = os.path.join(work_dir, "dam{:03d}".format(idx))
                job.update({"settings_path": stem + ".json", "out_path": stem + ".out.txt",
                            "err_path": stem + ".err.txt"})
                job["t0"] = _clock()
                settings = job["settings"]
                if job.get("result_path"):
                    settings = dict(settings)
                    settings[RESULT_KEY] = job["result_path"]
                try:
                    write_worker_settings(job["settings_path"], settings)
                    job["out"] = open(job["out_path"], "wb")
                    job["err"] = open(job["err_path"], "wb")
                    job["proc"] = popen(worker_command(exe, job["folder"], job["settings_path"]),
                                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=job["out"],
                                        stderr=job["err"], env=env, **kw)
                except OSError as e:
                    close(job)
                    if not started_any:
                        raise WorkerUnavailable("{}: {}".format(exe, e)) from e
                    running.append(job)
                    end(job, False, "the worker process could not be started: {}".format(e))
                    continue
                started_any = True
                running.append(job)
                if log:
                    log("{}: worker started ({} running)".format(job["name"], len(running)))
                say("{}: worker started".format(job["name"]))
            _sleep(_POLL_S)
            for job in list(running):
                rc = job["proc"].poll()
                if rc is None:
                    if timeout_s and _clock() - job["t0"] > timeout_s:
                        _terminate(job["proc"])
                        close(job)
                        tail = _tail(job["err_path"]) or _tail(job["out_path"])
                        end(job, False, "timed out after {:.0f} min - worker ended{}".format(
                            timeout_s / 60.0, ": " + tail if tail else ""))
                    continue
                if rc == 0:
                    end(job, True, "")
                else:
                    close(job)
                    tail = _tail(job["err_path"]) or _tail(job["out_path"])
                    end(job, False, "qgis_process ended with exit code {}: {}".format(
                        rc, tail or "no error text captured"))
            say()
    finally:
        for job in list(running):           # cancel or an error: leave nothing behind
            _terminate(job["proc"])
            close(job)
    return results


def mode_text(info):
    """One line naming how the watch / batch ran (log and report header)."""
    info = info or {}
    if info.get("mode") == "parallel":
        return "parallel - {} qgis_process worker(s) at a time ({}), {}".format(
            info.get("workers"), info.get("executable"),
            "no per-dam time limit" if not info.get("timeout_s")
            else "per-dam limit {:.0f} min".format(info["timeout_s"] / 60.0))
    if info.get("fallback_reason"):
        return "sequential in this QGIS session - {} workers were requested but {}".format(
            info.get("requested_workers"), info["fallback_reason"])
    return "sequential in this QGIS session (one dam after another)"


def clamp_workers(workers):
    """1 .. MAX_WORKERS (anything unreadable is 1)."""
    try:
        return max(1, min(MAX_WORKERS, int(workers)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
        return 1


def clean_timeout(timeout_s):
    """A per-dam limit in seconds; 0 = none (also for None, negative or
    unreadable values)."""
    try:
        t = float(timeout_s)
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
        return 0
    if not 0 < t < float("inf"):         # also NaN
        return 0
    return int(t) if t == int(t) else t


def _unsupported_settings(cfg_over):
    """Settings a worker process cannot be given - a parallel run would differ
    from a sequential one, so it is not used: layers and other objects; since
    v2.9 also pipeline settings a CONFIG_JSON file cannot carry (the dam's
    folder / scenarios / output folder, a wrongly typed value) when they differ
    from what the worker would use (the default)."""
    cfg_over = cfg_over or {}
    bad = {k for k, v in cfg_over.items()
           if v is not None and not isinstance(v, (bool, int, float, str))}
    try:
        from .pipeline import DEFAULTS
        from .processing_provider import worker_settings
        passed = worker_settings(cfg_over)
        for k, v in cfg_over.items():
            if k in DEFAULTS and k not in passed and v is not None and k not in bad:
                try:
                    same = v == DEFAULTS[k]
                except Exception:
                    same = False
                if not same:
                    bad.add(k)
    except Exception:           # the Processing module / pipeline not importable
        pass
    return sorted(bad)


def plan_mode(workers, cfg, timeout_s, qgis_process=None, info=None, blocked=None):
    """How a folder of dams is classified: fills (and returns) `info` with
    mode ("sequential" / "parallel"), requested_workers, workers, executable,
    fallback_reason, timeout_s and text (mode_text). Parallel needs
    `workers` > 1, the qgis_process executable (`qgis_process`, else
    find_qgis_process) and settings `cfg` a worker can receive; otherwise the
    mode is sequential and fallback_reason says why. `blocked` (text) forces
    the sequential mode for that reason."""
    workers = clamp_workers(workers)
    timeout_s = clean_timeout(timeout_s)
    state = info if info is not None else {}
    state.clear()
    state.update({"mode": "sequential", "requested_workers": workers, "workers": 1,
                  "executable": "", "fallback_reason": "", "timeout_s": timeout_s})
    if workers > 1:
        if blocked:
            exe, why = None, blocked
        else:
            exe, why = (qgis_process, "") if qgis_process else find_qgis_process()
        bad = _unsupported_settings(cfg)
        if exe and bad:
            exe, why = None, "the settings {} cannot be passed to worker processes".format(
                ", ".join(bad))
        if exe:
            state.update({"mode": "parallel", "workers": workers, "executable": exe})
        else:
            state["fallback_reason"] = why
    state["text"] = mode_text(state)
    return state


def fall_back(state, why):
    """Switch a planned parallel run to the sequential mode (reason `why`)."""
    state.update({"mode": "sequential", "workers": 1, "executable": "",
                  "fallback_reason": why})
    state["text"] = mode_text(state)
    return state


def watch_row(folder, batch_row, before, mark=None):
    """The watch row of one dam from its batch row (processing_provider.
    BATCH_FIELDS), its snapshot before the run and the file_mark of that
    snapshot before the run (None: there was none)."""
    from .helpers import dam_display_name
    name = dam_display_name(folder)
    b = batch_row
    if b is None or b.get("Status") in ("skipped", "failed"):
        return failed_row(name, folder, (b or {}).get("Status") or "skipped",
                          (b or {}).get("Message") or "not classified")
    after = HIS.read_snapshot(qa_folder(folder))
    if after is None:
        return failed_row(name, folder, "failed", "the classification finished but wrote "
                          "no Last_Run_Snapshot.json")
    if mark is not None and file_mark(snapshot_path(folder)) == mark:
        return failed_row(name, folder, "failed", "the classification finished but did not "
                          "write a new QA/Last_Run_Snapshot.json - not compared (see the "
                          "dam's run log)")
    return summarise(name, folder, before, after, read_changes(folder))


def run_watch(parent, cfg_over=None, progress=None, log=None, classify=None, workers=1,
              timeout_s=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S, info=None, qgis_process=None, popen=None):
    """Watch every dam folder under `parent`. Returns (rows, paths).
    `classify(parent, over, progress, log)` is processing_provider.batch_classify
    (a parameter so the watch can be tested without the Processing module; when
    given, the watch always runs sequentially).
    `workers` > 1 runs the dams as that many parallel qgis_process worker
    processes (see the module docstring) and falls back to the sequential mode
    when qgis_process is not found, this is no real QGIS, or `cfg_over` holds
    settings a child process cannot receive (layers). `timeout_s` is the limit
    per dam in that mode (0 = none). `info`, when a dict, is filled with the mode
    used: mode ("sequential" / "parallel"), requested_workers, workers, executable,
    fallback_reason, timeout_s, text. `qgis_process` (a path) skips the search
    for the executable; `popen` replaces subprocess.Popen (tests).
    Both modes also write Batch_Hazard_Classification.csv (v2.9; its path is
    paths["batch"])."""
    if not parent or not os.path.isdir(parent):
        raise ValueError("Folder not found: {}".format(parent))
    folders = dam_folders(parent)
    befores = {f: read_before(f) for f in folders}
    marks = {f: file_mark(snapshot_path(f)) for f in folders}
    state = info if info is not None else {}
    cfg = fresh_data_config(cfg_over)
    if classify is None:
        from .processing_provider import batch_classify
        batch_rows, _csv = batch_classify(
            parent, cfg, progress=progress, log=log, workers=workers, timeout_s=timeout_s,
            info=state, qgis_process=qgis_process, popen=popen, label="Creep watch",
            worker_log=WATCH_WORKER_LOG)
    else:
        plan_mode(workers, cfg, timeout_s, info=state,
                  blocked="a custom classify function is used")
        if log:
            log(">>> Creep watch mode: " + state["text"])
        batch_rows, _csv = classify(parent, cfg, progress=progress, log=log)
    by_folder = {r.get("Folder"): r for r in batch_rows or []}
    rows = [watch_row(f, by_folder.get(f), befores.get(f), marks.get(f)) for f in folders]
    paths = write_reports(parent, rows, mode=state["text"])
    if _csv:
        paths["batch"] = _csv                   # Batch_Hazard_Classification.csv
    return rows, paths
```

## `webexport.py`

```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""v2.9.0: KMZ (Google Earth) and GeoJSON (web maps) copies of the EAP layers.

export_layers(layers_or_paths, out_folder) writes, per vector layer:

* <name>.geojson - RFC 7946: WGS 84 longitude / latitude (EPSG:4326, the
  layer is reprojected with the project's transform context), coordinates
  rounded to GEOJSON_PRECISION decimals (about 1 cm), written by
  QgsVectorFileWriter with the OGR "GeoJSON" driver.
* <name>.kmz - a zip holding doc.kml, written by QgsVectorFileWriter with
  the OGR "KML" driver (LIBKML when KML fails). Each placemark gets a
  readable name (field KML_Name, see feature_label(): the notification list
  shows "12. 123 Main St (1:30)", contours "Arrival 2 h", map sheets "Sheet 3",
  other layers their Name / Address / Label field) and each layer a simple
  colour (arrival-band polygons: the colours of the arrival-band raster).

export_eap_web(eap_folder, dam_name) finds the EAP layers the run wrote
(outputs/EAP/EAP_*.gpkg - notification list, travel-time table, channel
centerline, arrival contours, map sheets -, EAP_Termination_Point.gpkg in
outputs/QA, and EAP_Arrival_Bands*.tif turned into polygons - the flooded
area by arrival time, i.e. the inundation boundary - where GDAL can) and
writes them to outputs/EAP/Web/, plus one KMZ with every layer as a folder.

One bad layer never stops the others: it is logged and its entry says why.
Nothing here changes the layers or the EAP files.
"""

import os
import re
import shutil
import tempfile
import zipfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

from qgis.core import (
    QgsVectorLayer, QgsVectorFileWriter, QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem, QgsCoordinateTransform,
    QgsCoordinateTransformContext, QgsFeatureRequest, QgsField,
)

from .compat import FT_STRING, WRITER_NO_ERROR, MSG_WARNING, NULL, enum_value
from .helpers import log_message, prepare_output_path

WEB_SUBDIR = "Web"
GEOJSON_PRECISION = 7                    # decimals of a degree (RFC 7946 default)
KML_DRIVERS = ("KML", "LIBKML")
LABEL_FIELD = "KML_Name"
ALL_LAYERS_NAME = "EAP_All_Layers"
MAX_POLYGONIZE_CELLS = 60e6              # larger arrival-band rasters are not converted

KML_NS = "http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2"
_NS = {"": KML_NS, "gx": "http://www.google.com/kml/ext/2.2",
       "atom": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom",
       "xal": "urn:oasis:names:tc:ciq:xsdschema:xAL:2.0"}

# the layers export_eap_web looks for, in this order (base-name prefixes)
EAP_LAYER_ORDER = ("EAP_Notification_List", "EAP_Travel_Time", "EAP_Termination_Point",
                   "EAP_Channel_Centerline", "EAP_Arrival_Contours", "EAP_Arrival_Bands",
                   "EAP_Map_Sheets")

# simple per-layer colours (#rrggbb); None = per feature (arrival bands)
LAYER_COLORS = (("EAP_Notification_List", "#d7301f"), ("EAP_Travel_Time", "#fd8d3c"),
                ("EAP_Termination_Point", "#6a3d9a"), ("EAP_Channel_Centerline", "#1f78b4"),
                ("EAP_Arrival_Contours", "#08519c"), ("EAP_Arrival_Bands", None),
                ("EAP_Map_Sheets", "#525252"))
DEFAULT_COLOR = "#e31a1c"
_OUTLINE_ONLY = ("EAP_Map_Sheets",)

_GENERIC_NAME_FIELDS = ("name", "label", "address", "prop_addr", "full_addr", "site_name",
                        "facility", "title", "item", "status", "id")

for _p, _u in _NS.items():
    try:
        ET.register_namespace(_p, _u)
    except ValueError:
        pass


def _log(log):
    return log or (lambda m: log_message(m))


def safe_name(name):
    """A file-name-safe version of a layer / dam name."""
    s = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "_", str(name or "")).strip("._")
    return s[:80] or "layer"


def _family(base):
    for pre in EAP_LAYER_ORDER:
        if base.startswith(pre):
            return pre
    return ""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ labels --
def _txt(v):
    if v is None or v is NULL:
        return ""
    try:
        if v.isNull():                       # QVariant (Qt5 NULL)
            return ""
    except AttributeError:
        pass
    s = str(v).strip()
    return "" if s.upper() in ("NULL", "NONE") else s


def _num(v):
    s = _txt(v)
    try:
        f = float(s)
        return "{:g}".format(f)
    except ValueError:
        return s


def feature_label(base, attrs, fallback=""):
    """Placemark name of a feature of layer `base` (attrs: {field: value},
    any case)."""
    a = dict((str(k).lower(), v) for k, v in (attrs or {}).items())

    def g(k):
        return _txt(a.get(k.lower()))
    fam = _family(base)
    if fam == "EAP_Notification_List":
        what = g("Address") or g("Name") or g("Category") or g("Type")
        t = g("Arrival_hhmm")
        return "{}{}{}".format("{}. ".format(_num(a.get("order"))) if g("Order") else "",
                               what or fallback, " ({})".format(t) if t else "")
    if fam == "EAP_Travel_Time":
        what = g("Name") or g("Item")
        rm = _num(a.get("river_mile"))
        t = g("Arrival_hhmm")
        return "{}{}{}".format("RM {}: ".format(rm) if rm else "", what or fallback,
                               " ({})".format(t) if t else "")
    if fam == "EAP_Arrival_Contours":
        v = _num(a.get("arrival_hr"))
        return "Arrival {} h".format(v) if v else (fallback or "Arrival contour")
    if fam == "EAP_Arrival_Bands":
        lbl = g("Arrival")
        if not lbl:
            try:
                from .eap import band_labels
                lbl = dict(band_labels()).get(int(float(g("Class"))), "")
            except (ValueError, ImportError):
                lbl = ""
        return "Arrival {}".format(lbl) if lbl else (fallback or "Flooded area")
    if fam == "EAP_Map_Sheets":
        s = _num(a.get("sheet"))
        return "Sheet {}".format(s) if s else fallback
    if fam == "EAP_Termination_Point":
        st, rm = g("Status"), _num(a.get("river_mile"))
        return "Termination point{}{}".format(" - {}".format(st) if st else "",
                                               " (RM {})".format(rm) if rm else "")
    if fam == "EAP_Channel_Centerline":
        return "Channel centerline" + (" ({})".format(g("Source")) if g("Source") else "")
    for k in _GENERIC_NAME_FIELDS:
        v = g(k)
        if v:
            return v
    return fallback


def _labelled_copy(layer, base):
    """Memory copy of `layer` with the placemark name in LABEL_FIELD (the
    layer itself is not changed)."""
    mem = layer.materialize(QgsFeatureRequest())
    idx = mem.fields().indexOf(LABEL_FIELD)
    if idx < 0:
        mem.dataProvider().addAttributes([QgsField(LABEL_FIELD, FT_STRING)])
        mem.updateFields()
        idx = mem.fields().indexOf(LABEL_FIELD)
    names = [f.name() for f in mem.fields()]
    changes = {}
    title = base.replace("_", " ")
    for i, f in enumerate(mem.getFeatures()):
        attrs = dict(zip(names, f.attributes()))
        changes[f.id()] = {idx: feature_label(base, attrs, "{} {}".format(title, i + 1))[:250]}
    if changes:
        mem.dataProvider().changeAttributeValues(changes)
    return mem


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- writing --
def _ctx():
    try:
        from qgis.core import QgsProject
        return QgsProject.instance().transformContext()
    except Exception:
        return QgsCoordinateTransformContext()


def _to_wgs84(layer, ctx):
    """QgsCoordinateTransform layer CRS -> EPSG:4326 (None: already 4326)."""
    dst = QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem("EPSG:4326")
    src = layer.crs()
    if src is None or not src.isValid():
        raise ValueError("the layer has no CRS - it cannot be placed on a web map")
    if src.authid() == "EPSG:4326":
        return None
    return QgsCoordinateTransform(src, dst, ctx)


def _write(layer, path, ctx, driver, ct, layer_name, layer_opts=(), ds_opts=()):
    opts = QgsVectorFileWriter.SaveVectorOptions()
    opts.driverName = driver
    opts.fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
    opts.layerName = layer_name
    opts.layerOptions = list(layer_opts)
    opts.datasourceOptions = list(ds_opts)
    if ct is not None:
        opts.ct = ct
    res = QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormatV3(layer, path, ctx, opts)
    code = res[0] if isinstance(res, tuple) else res
    if enum_value(code) != enum_value(WRITER_NO_ERROR):
        msg = res[1] if isinstance(res, tuple) and len(res) > 1 else ""
        raise RuntimeError("{} writer: {} ({})".format(driver, msg or "failed",
                                                       enum_value(code)))
    return path


def write_geojson(layer, out_path, ctx=None):
    """RFC 7946 GeoJSON (EPSG:4326, GEOJSON_PRECISION decimals). Returns the
    path written (another name when the file was locked)."""
    ctx = ctx or _ctx()
    ct = _to_wgs84(layer, ctx)
    path = prepare_output_path(out_path)
    return _write(layer, path, ctx, "GeoJSON", ct,
                  os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(out_path))[0],
                  layer_opts=("RFC7946=YES", "COORDINATE_PRECISION={}".format(GEOJSON_PRECISION),
                              "WRITE_BBOX=NO"))


def write_kmz(layer, out_path, base=None, ctx=None):
    """KMZ (zip with doc.kml) of the layer, placemarks named by
    feature_label(), coloured per layer. Returns the path written."""
    ctx = ctx or _ctx()
    base = base or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(out_path))[0]
    ct = _to_wgs84(layer, ctx)
    folder = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(out_path))
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="_kml_", dir=folder)
    try:
        src = _labelled_copy(layer, base)
        kml = os.path.join(work, "doc.kml")
        errors = []
        title = _family(base).replace("_", " ") or base.replace("_", " ")
        for driver in KML_DRIVERS:
            try:
                _write_kml(src, kml, ctx, driver, ct, title)
                break
            except Exception as e:                  # noqa - next driver
                errors.append("{}: {}".format(driver, e))
                if os.path.exists(kml):
                    os.remove(kml)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("; ".join(errors))
        style_kml(kml, base)
        path = prepare_output_path(out_path)
        tmp = path + ".part"
        with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
            z.write(kml, "doc.kml")
        os.replace(tmp, path)
        return path
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)


def _write_kml(layer, path, ctx, driver, ct, title):
    if driver == "LIBKML":
        try:
            from osgeo import gdal
            old = gdal.GetConfigOption("LIBKML_NAME_FIELD")
            gdal.SetConfigOption("LIBKML_NAME_FIELD", LABEL_FIELD)
        except Exception:
            gdal = old = None
        try:
            return _write(layer, path, ctx, driver, ct, title)
        finally:
            if gdal is not None:
                gdal.SetConfigOption("LIBKML_NAME_FIELD", old)
    return _write(layer, path, ctx, driver, ct, title,
                  ds_opts=("NameField={}".format(LABEL_FIELD),))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ styling --
def _kml_color(rgb, alpha=255):
    """#rrggbb -> KML aabbggrr."""
    h = rgb.lstrip("#")
    return "{:02x}{}{}{}".format(int(alpha), h[4:6], h[2:4], h[0:2])


def _style_el(sid, rgb, outline_only=False):
    st = ET.Element("{%s}Style" % KML_NS, {"id": sid})
    for tag, kids in (("IconStyle", (("color", _kml_color(rgb)), ("scale", "1.1"))),
                      ("LabelStyle", (("scale", "0.8"),)),
                      ("LineStyle", (("color", _kml_color(rgb)), ("width", "2.5"))),
                      ("PolyStyle", (("color", _kml_color(rgb, 0 if outline_only else 102)),
                                     ("fill", "0" if outline_only else "1"),
                                     ("outline", "1")))):
        e = ET.SubElement(st, "{%s}%s" % (KML_NS, tag))
        for k, v in kids:
            ET.SubElement(e, "{%s}%s" % (KML_NS, k)).text = v
    return st


_LEAD = ("name", "visibility", "open", "address", "phoneNumber", "Snippet", "description")


def _insert_after_lead(parent, el):
    i = 0
    for i, child in enumerate(list(parent)):
        if child.tag.split("}")[-1] not in _LEAD:
            break
    else:
        i = len(parent)
    parent.insert(i, el)


def _band_class(pm):
    for sd in pm.iter("{%s}SimpleData" % KML_NS):
        if sd.get("name", "").lower() == "class":
            try:
                return int(float(sd.text or ""))
            except ValueError:
                return None
    return None


def style_kml(kml_path, base):
    """Give the placemarks of a KML file written by OGR a colour (Style +
    styleUrl). Best effort: the file stays as it is when it cannot be parsed."""
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(kml_path)
        root = tree.getroot()
        doc = root.find("{%s}Document" % KML_NS)
        if doc is None:
            return False
        fam = _family(base)
        color = dict(LAYER_COLORS).get(fam, DEFAULT_COLOR) if fam else DEFAULT_COLOR
        sid = "s_" + safe_name(base)
        styles = []
        if fam == "EAP_Arrival_Bands":
            from .eap import BAND_COLORS
            per = {}
            for i, rgb in enumerate(BAND_COLORS):
                per[i + 1] = "{}_{}".format(sid, i + 1)
                styles.append(_style_el(per[i + 1], rgb))
            styles.append(_style_el(sid, DEFAULT_COLOR))
        else:
            per = None
            styles.append(_style_el(sid, color, outline_only=fam in _OUTLINE_ONLY))
        for st in reversed(styles):
            _insert_after_lead(doc, st)
        for pm in root.iter("{%s}Placemark" % KML_NS):
            if pm.find("{%s}styleUrl" % KML_NS) is not None:
                continue
            use = sid
            if per is not None:
                use = per.get(_band_class(pm), sid)
            su = ET.Element("{%s}styleUrl" % KML_NS)
            su.text = "#" + use
            _insert_after_lead(pm, su)
        tree.write(kml_path, encoding="utf-8", xml_declaration=True)
        return True
    except Exception:                                   # noqa - colours are optional
        return False


def merge_kmz(kmz_paths, out_path, title):
    """One KMZ with the documents of several KMZ files as folders (styles and
    schemas kept). Returns the path, or None when nothing could be merged."""
    doc = ET.Element("{%s}Document" % KML_NS)
    ET.SubElement(doc, "{%s}name" % KML_NS).text = title
    heads, folders = [], []
    for p in kmz_paths:
        try:
            with zipfile.ZipFile(p) as z:
                root = ET.fromstring(z.read("doc.kml"))
            d = root.find("{%s}Document" % KML_NS)
            if d is None:
                continue
            kids = [c for c in d if c.tag.split("}")[-1] not in ("name", "open")]
            heads += [c for c in kids if c.tag.split("}")[-1] in ("Style", "StyleMap", "Schema")]
            body = [c for c in kids if c.tag.split("}")[-1] not in ("Style", "StyleMap",
                                                                    "Schema")]
            if len(body) == 1 and body[0].tag.split("}")[-1] == "Folder":
                folders.append(body[0])
            elif body:
                f = ET.Element("{%s}Folder" % KML_NS)
                ET.SubElement(f, "{%s}name" % KML_NS).text = \
                    os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0]
                f.extend(body)
                folders.append(f)
        except Exception:                               # noqa - skip that one
            continue
    if not folders:
        return None
    doc.extend(heads + folders)
    root = ET.Element("{%s}kml" % KML_NS)
    root.append(doc)
    path = prepare_output_path(out_path)
    tmp = path + ".part"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        z.writestr("doc.kml", b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>\n' +
                   ET.tostring(root, encoding="utf-8"))
    os.replace(tmp, path)
    return path


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ public --
def _items(layers_or_paths):
    """[(name, layer or path)] from layers, paths, (name, x) pairs or a dict."""
    if isinstance(layers_or_paths, dict):
        return list(layers_or_paths.items())
    if isinstance(layers_or_paths, (str, QgsVectorLayer)):
        layers_or_paths = [layers_or_paths]
    out = []
    for it in layers_or_paths or []:
        if isinstance(it, (tuple, list)) and len(it) == 2:
            out.append((str(it[0]), it[1]))
        elif isinstance(it, str):
            out.append((os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(it.split("|")[0]))[0], it))
        else:
            try:
                out.append((it.name(), it))
            except Exception:
                out.append(("layer", it))
    return out


def export_layers(layers_or_paths, out_folder, formats=("kmz", "geojson"), name_prefix="",
                  log=None):
    """KMZ and / or GeoJSON copies of vector layers (QgsVectorLayer, file paths,
    (name, layer-or-path) pairs or {name: layer-or-path}) in out_folder.
    Returns {name: {"kmz": path or None, "geojson": path or None,
    "features": n, "error": "" or why}} - name without the prefix. Never
    raises for one layer."""
    log = _log(log)
    result = {}
    try:
        os.makedirs(out_folder, exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as e:
        log("Web export: folder {} cannot be made ({})".format(out_folder, e))
        return result
    ctx = _ctx()
    formats = tuple(f.lower() for f in (formats or ()))
    for name, src in _items(layers_or_paths):
        base = name
        k = 2
        while base in result:
            base = "{}_{}".format(name, k)
            k += 1
        entry = result[base] = {"kmz": None, "geojson": None, "features": 0, "error": ""}
        try:
            lyr = src
            if isinstance(src, str):
                lyr = QgsVectorLayer(src, base, "ogr")
            if lyr is None or not lyr.isValid():
                raise ValueError("cannot be opened")
            entry["features"] = n = lyr.featureCount()
            if not n:
                raise ValueError("no features")
            fname = safe_name(name_prefix + base)
            if "geojson" in formats:
                try:
                    entry["geojson"] = write_geojson(
                        lyr, os.path.join(out_folder, fname + ".geojson"), ctx)
                except Exception as e:              # noqa
                    entry["error"] += "GeoJSON: {}; ".format(e)
            if "kmz" in formats:
                try:
                    entry["kmz"] = write_kmz(lyr, os.path.join(out_folder, fname + ".kmz"),
                                             base=base, ctx=ctx)
                except Exception as e:              # noqa
                    entry["error"] += "KMZ: {}; ".format(e)
            entry["error"] = entry["error"].rstrip("; ")
        except Exception as e:                      # noqa - one bad layer
            entry["error"] = str(e) or e.__class__.__name__
        if entry["error"]:
            log("Web export of {}: {}".format(base, entry["error"]))
    return result


def find_eap_layers(eap_folder):
    """[(name, path)] of the EAP vector layers of a run: EAP_*.gpkg in the EAP
    folder, EAP_Termination_Point*.gpkg in the QA folder beside it (or the
    same folder - runs without sub-folders), in EAP_LAYER_ORDER."""
    found = {}
    folders = [eap_folder, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(eap_folder)), "QA")]
    for folder in folders:
        try:
            names = sorted(os.listdir(folder))
        except OSError:
            continue
        for f in names:
            stem, ext = os.path.splitext(f)
            if ext.lower() != ".gpkg" or not stem.startswith("EAP_") or stem in found:
                continue
            if folder != eap_folder and not stem.startswith("EAP_Termination_Point"):
                continue
            found[stem] = os.path.join(folder, f)

    def order(stem):
        fam = _family(stem)
        return (EAP_LAYER_ORDER.index(fam) if fam else len(EAP_LAYER_ORDER), stem)
    return [(s, found[s]) for s in sorted(found, key=order)]


def _band_rasters(eap_folder):
    try:
        return [os.path.join(eap_folder, f) for f in sorted(os.listdir(eap_folder))
                if f.startswith("EAP_Arrival_Bands") and f.lower().endswith(".tif")]
    except OSError:
        return []


def polygonize_bands(tif, name=None):
    """The arrival-band raster as polygons - the flooded area by arrival time
    (the inundation boundary) - in a QGIS memory layer (fields Class, Arrival;
    the raster's CRS). GDAL Polygonize into an OGR memory layer: no file is
    written. Returns (layer, "") or (None, why)."""
    from osgeo import gdal, ogr
    from qgis.core import QgsRasterLayer, QgsFeature, QgsGeometry
    from .compat import WKB_POLYGON, FT_INT
    from .helpers import create_memory_layer, gdal_exceptions
    from .eap import band_labels
    if not hasattr(gdal, "Polygonize"):
        return None, "GDAL Polygonize is not available"
    drv = ogr.GetDriverByName("MEM") or ogr.GetDriverByName("Memory")
    if drv is None or not hasattr(drv, "CreateDataSource"):
        return None, "the OGR memory driver is not available"
    name = name or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(tif))[0]
    rl = QgsRasterLayer(tif, name)
    if not rl.isValid():
        return None, "the raster cannot be opened"
    labels = dict(band_labels())
    with gdal_exceptions():
        src = gdal.Open(tif, gdal.GA_ReadOnly)
        if src.RasterXSize * float(src.RasterYSize) > MAX_POLYGONIZE_CELLS:
            return None, "{:,} x {:,} cells - too large to convert here (open the .tif in " \
                         "QGIS instead)".format(src.RasterXSize, src.RasterYSize)
        band = src.GetRasterBand(1)
        ds = drv.CreateDataSource("bands")
        olyr = ds.CreateLayer("bands", None, ogr.wkbPolygon)
        olyr.CreateField(ogr.FieldDefn("Class", ogr.OFTInteger))
        gdal.Polygonize(band, band.GetMaskBand(), olyr, 0, [])
        mem = create_memory_layer(name, WKB_POLYGON, rl.crs(),
                                  [QgsField("Class", FT_INT), QgsField("Arrival", FT_STRING)])
        feats = []
        olyr.ResetReading()
        of = olyr.GetNextFeature()
        while of is not None:
            g = QgsGeometry.fromWkb(bytes(of.GetGeometryRef().ExportToWkb()))
            cls = of.GetField("Class")
            f = QgsFeature(mem.fields())
            f.setGeometry(g)
            f.setAttributes([cls, labels.get(cls, "")])
            feats.append(f)
            of = olyr.GetNextFeature()
        olyr = ds = band = src = None
    if not feats:
        return None, "no flooded cell with an arrival time"
    mem.dataProvider().addFeatures(feats)
    mem.updateExtents()
    return mem, ""


def export_eap_web(eap_folder, dam_name, log=None, formats=("kmz", "geojson"),
                   bands=True):
    """KMZ / GeoJSON of the run's EAP layers in <eap_folder>/Web (see the
    module text), file names prefixed with the dam name, plus
    <dam>_EAP_All_Layers.kmz with every layer. Returns export_layers()'s dict
    (with an ALL_LAYERS_NAME entry for the combined KMZ). Never raises."""
    log = _log(log)
    result = {}
    try:
        out = os.path.join(eap_folder, WEB_SUBDIR)
        items = find_eap_layers(eap_folder)
        if bands:
            for tif in _band_rasters(eap_folder):
                stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(tif))[0]
                try:
                    lyr, why = polygonize_bands(tif, stem)
                    if lyr is not None:
                        items.append((stem, lyr))
                    else:
                        log("Web export: {} not converted to polygons ({})".format(stem, why))
                except Exception as e:                  # noqa
                    log("Web export: {} not converted to polygons ({})".format(stem, e))
        if not items:
            log("Web export: no EAP layers in {}".format(eap_folder))
            return result
        prefix = safe_name(dam_name) + "_" if dam_name else ""
        result = export_layers(items, out, formats=formats, name_prefix=prefix, log=log)
        kmzs = [v["kmz"] for v in result.values() if v.get("kmz")]
        if len(kmzs) > 1 and "kmz" in formats:
            try:
                p = merge_kmz(kmzs, os.path.join(out, safe_name(prefix + ALL_LAYERS_NAME) +
                                                 ".kmz"),
                              "{} - EAP layers".format(dam_name) if dam_name else "EAP layers")
                if p:
                    result[ALL_LAYERS_NAME] = {"kmz": p, "geojson": None,
                                               "features": sum(v.get("features", 0)
                                                               for v in result.values()),
                                               "error": ""}
            except Exception as e:                      # noqa
                log("Web export: the combined KMZ was not written ({})".format(e))
        ok = [k for k, v in result.items() if v.get("kmz") or v.get("geojson")]
        log("Web export: {} of {} EAP layer(s) written to {}".format(
            len([k for k in ok if k != ALL_LAYERS_NAME]), len(items), out))
    except Exception as e:                              # noqa
        log("Web export failed: {}".format(e))
    return result


def summary_lines(result, folder_label="EAP/Web"):
    """Run-log / summary lines of an export_eap_web() result."""
    lines = []
    for name, v in (result or {}).items():
        files = [os.path.basename(v[k]) for k in ("kmz", "geojson") if v.get(k)]
        if files:
            lines.append("{}: {} ({})".format(folder_label, ", ".join(files),
                                               "{} feature(s)".format(v.get("features", 0))))
        elif v.get("error"):
            lines.append("{}: {} not exported - {}".format(folder_label, name, v["error"]))
    return lines
```

## `webmap.py`

```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Web-map link for the Review tab ("Open in web map").

The engineer opens the selected structure's location in the web browser for
a street-level look (street view, recent imagery, business names). The
default is the Google Maps URLs "search" action, which needs no API key:

    https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={lat}%2C{lon}

(documented at https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/urls/get-started:
latitude first, the comma encoded as %2C). Another address can be set with
WEBMAP_URL_TEMPLATE in constants.py / the data-source file: an http(s)
address with {lat} and {lon} in it, e.g. the Google Street View panorama
https://www.google.com/maps/@?api=1&map_action=pano&viewpoint={lat}%2C{lon}
(rural North Dakota often has no panorama, so the search pin is the default).
An address that is not usable is ignored (one line in the log) and the
default is used.

Opening the link sends the structure's coordinates to that web site; nothing
else about the study leaves the computer."""

import math
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from qgis.core import (
    QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem, QgsCoordinateTransform, QgsPointXY, QgsProject,
)

from . import constants as C
from .helpers import log_message
from .compat import MSG_WARNING

DEFAULT_TEMPLATE = "https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={lat}%2C{lon}"
WGS84 = "EPSG:4326"
DECIMALS = 6                     # ~0.1 m - plenty for "which building is it"
_warned = set()                  # bad templates already reported (one log line each)


def template_problem(template):
    """Why a web-map address cannot be used (text), or None when it can."""
    if not isinstance(template, str):
        return "the address is not text"
    t = template.strip()
    if not t:
        return "the address is empty"
    try:
        parts = urlparse(t)
    except ValueError as e:
        return "not a web address ({})".format(e)
    if parts.scheme.lower() not in ("http", "https") or not parts.netloc:
        return "only http:// or https:// addresses are opened"
    if "{lat}" not in t or "{lon}" not in t:
        return "the address needs {lat} and {lon}"
    return None


def configured_template():
    """WEBMAP_URL_TEMPLATE from constants / the data-source file, or None."""
    return getattr(C, "WEBMAP_URL_TEMPLATE", None) or None


def usable_template(template=None):
    """The template to use: `template` (or the configured one) when it is
    valid, otherwise DEFAULT_TEMPLATE (a bad one is logged once)."""
    if template is None:
        template = configured_template()
    if template is None:
        return DEFAULT_TEMPLATE
    problem = template_problem(template)
    if problem is None:
        return template.strip()
    key = str(template)
    if key not in _warned:
        _warned.add(key)
        log_message("Web map address {!r} not used ({}) - using {}".format(
            template, problem, DEFAULT_TEMPLATE), MSG_WARNING)
    return DEFAULT_TEMPLATE


def valid_lonlat(lon, lat):
    try:
        lon, lat = float(lon), float(lat)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False
    return (math.isfinite(lon) and math.isfinite(lat) and -180.0 <= lon <= 180.0 and
            -90.0 <= lat <= 90.0)


def url_for(lat, lon, template=None):
    """The web-map address of a WGS 84 location (latitude first, as in the
    template's {lat} / {lon}). Raises ValueError for an impossible location."""
    if not valid_lonlat(lon, lat):
        raise ValueError("not a longitude / latitude: {}, {}".format(lon, lat))
    fmt = "{:.%df}" % DECIMALS
    # str.replace, not str.format: a template may hold other braces
    return (usable_template(template).replace("{lat}", fmt.format(float(lat)))
            .replace("{lon}", fmt.format(float(lon))))


def lonlat_of(rec, crs, ctx=None):
    """(lon, lat) in WGS 84 of a structure record (its representative point
    in the analysis CRS `crs`), or None when it cannot be located."""
    from .review import rep_point
    p = rep_point(rec)
    if p is None or crs is None:
        return None
    try:
        if not crs.isValid():
            return None               # projected numbers must never be read as degrees
        if ctx is None:
            ctx = QgsProject.instance().transformContext()
        xf = QgsCoordinateTransform(crs, QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem(WGS84), ctx)
        q = QgsPointXY(p.x(), p.y())
        if not xf.isShortCircuited():
            q = xf.transform(q)
        lon, lat = q.x(), q.y()
    except Exception as e:
        log_message("Web map: structure {} could not be located in WGS 84 ({})".format(
            rec.get("id", "?"), e), MSG_WARNING)
        return None
    return (lon, lat) if valid_lonlat(lon, lat) else None


def url_of_structure(rec, crs, ctx=None, template=None):
    """The web-map address of a structure, or None when it cannot be located."""
    ll = lonlat_of(rec, crs, ctx)
    if ll is None:
        return None
    return url_for(ll[1], ll[0], template)
```

## `damsuite/__init__.py`

```python
"""damsuite - the shared package of the ND dam suite (ND Dam Hazard Classification Helper,
ND Dam Breach Runner, ND Dam Breach Screening).

Pure Python 3.9+ standard library: no QGIS, no numpy, no Qt. Importable anywhere.

The master copy lives in the suite folder; each plugin carries a byte-identical copy as a
sub-package (`<plugin>/damsuite/`) written by `sync_damsuite.py`, which also writes
`damsuite/FILES.json` = {file name: sha256 of its bytes} for every .py file of the package.
Never edit a vendored copy: edit the master and run the sync.

Modules:
  dam_record  one record per dam (<dam folder>/dam.json) shared by the three plugins
  versions    version checks between the plugins at start-up
  chain       model -> classification fingerprint chain (raster digests vs the runner's
              run_manifest.json)

`selfcheck()` compares this package's files with FILES.json and returns a list of problems
("missing: x.py", "changed: x.py", "unexpected file: x.py"); [] means the copy is intact.
The comparison is on raw bytes (a CRLF conversion counts as a change).

Nothing here has been run inside a real QGIS; the QGIS-facing part (versions.installed) is
written defensively and returns None on any failure.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os

from . import chain, dam_record, versions   # noqa: F401  (sub-modules, relative imports only)

SUITE_VERSION = "1.0.0"
FILES_NAME = "FILES.json"

__all__ = ["SUITE_VERSION", "FILES_NAME", "selfcheck", "package_files", "chain", "dam_record",
           "versions"]


def package_files(folder=None):
    """{file name: sha256} of the .py files directly in the package folder (sorted)."""
    folder = folder or os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    out = {}
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
        p = os.path.join(folder, name)
        if name.endswith(".py") and os.path.isfile(p):
            with open(p, "rb") as f:
                out[name] = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
    return out


def selfcheck(folder=None):
    """Problems of this package copy against its FILES.json; [] = OK.

    `folder` defaults to this package's own folder (the optional argument is for tests)."""
    folder = folder or os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    fpath = os.path.join(folder, FILES_NAME)
    if not os.path.isfile(fpath):
        return ["FILES.json missing"]
    try:
        with open(fpath, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            expected = json.load(f)
        if not isinstance(expected, dict):
            raise ValueError("not a JSON object")
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        return ["FILES.json unreadable: {}".format(e)]
    actual = package_files(folder)
    problems = []
    for name in sorted(expected):
        if name not in actual:
            problems.append("missing: {}".format(name))
        elif actual[name] != expected[name]:
            problems.append("changed: {}".format(name))
    for name in sorted(set(actual) - set(expected)):
        problems.append("unexpected file: {}".format(name))
    return problems
```

## `damsuite/chain.py`

```python
"""Model -> classification fingerprint chain.

The ND Dam Breach Runner writes `<dam folder>/_breach_model/run_manifest.json` after each run:
software versions, input files and output rasters with their digests, and a digest of the
manifest itself. This module checks that the rasters a hazard classification read are the
rasters that run wrote.

`file_digest`, `_canonical` and `digest_of` reproduce nd_breach_runner/core/provenance.py
exactly (same keys, same 8 MB start / middle / end sampling above `FULL_HASH_LIMIT`, same
canonical JSON), so digests compare directly with the runner's manifest. The suite's tests
prove the equality against the runner's module; if the runner's algorithm changes, change
it here too.

compare_rasters decisions:
  * `classified` is {role: path}; a relative path is taken relative to `dam_folder`.
  * The manifest's "outputs" are searched first, then its "inputs" (the note says so).
  * Match by digest first (sha256, and size when both are recorded) -> "MATCH"; then by file
    name (case-insensitive) -> "DIFFERENT"; then by role vs label ("base_depth" ~ "baseline
    depth", "incr_depth" ~ "incremental depth") -> "DIFFERENT"; else "NOT IN MANIFEST".
  * A classified raster that no longer exists gets status "MISSING" (an addition to the
    spec's three statuses: nothing can be compared).
  * A recorded manifest path that does not exist is looked up as <dam_folder>/<file name>
    (as the runner's verify_manifest does when the dam folder moved).
Nothing here needs QGIS.
"""
import datetime
import glob
import hashlib
import json
import os

FULL_HASH_LIMIT = 2 * 1024 ** 3        # as nd_breach_runner/core/provenance.py
PIECE = 8 * 1024 ** 2                  # as nd_breach_runner/core/provenance.py
MANIFEST_NAME = "run_manifest.json"
MODEL_FOLDER = "_breach_model"
STATUSES = ("MATCH", "DIFFERENT", "NOT IN MANIFEST", "MISSING")
_cache = {}


def sha256_file(path):
    """SHA-256 (hex) of the whole file."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


def file_digest(path, full_limit=FULL_HASH_LIMIT):
    """{"sha256", "size", "mtime", "sampled"} of a file, or {"missing": True}.

    Identical to the ND Dam Breach Runner's core/provenance.file_digest."""
    try:
        st = os.stat(path)
    except OSError:
        return {"missing": True}
    key = (os.path.abspath(path), st.st_size, st.st_mtime_ns, full_limit)
    if key in _cache:
        return dict(_cache[key])
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    sampled = st.st_size > full_limit
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            if not sampled:
                for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
                    h.update(block)
            else:
                h.update(str(st.st_size).encode())
                for pos in (0, max(0, st.st_size // 2 - PIECE // 2), max(0, st.st_size - PIECE)):
                    f.seek(pos)
                    h.update(f.read(PIECE))
    except OSError as e:
        return {"missing": True, "error": str(e)}
    out = {"sha256": h.hexdigest(), "size": st.st_size,
           "mtime": datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(st.st_mtime).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
           "sampled": sampled}
    _cache[key] = dict(out)
    return out


def _canonical(obj):
    return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, default=str, separators=(",", ":"))


def digest_of(manifest):
    """The runner's manifest digest: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON without "manifest_sha256"."""
    body = {k: v for k, v in manifest.items() if k != "manifest_sha256"}
    return hashlib.sha256(_canonical(body).encode()).hexdigest()


def find_runner_manifest(dam_folder):
    """Newest run_manifest.json of a dam folder: <dam>/_breach_model/, one folder level
    further down (<dam>/<run>/_breach_model/), or the folder itself when it is the model
    folder. A manifest file path is returned as given. None when there is none."""
    if not dam_folder:
        return None
    if os.path.isfile(dam_folder):
        return dam_folder if os.path.basename(dam_folder).lower() == MANIFEST_NAME else None
    cands = [os.path.join(dam_folder, MODEL_FOLDER, MANIFEST_NAME),
             os.path.join(dam_folder, MANIFEST_NAME)]
    cands += glob.glob(os.path.join(glob.escape(dam_folder), "*", MODEL_FOLDER, MANIFEST_NAME))
    found = []
    for p in cands:
        try:
            if os.path.isfile(p):
                found.append((os.path.getmtime(p), p))
        except OSError:
            pass
    if not found:
        return None
    return max(found)[1]


def read_runner_manifest(path):
    """The manifest dict. Raises OSError, or ValueError when it is not a JSON object."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        m = json.load(f)
    if not isinstance(m, dict):
        raise ValueError("{} is not a JSON object".format(path))
    return m


def manifest_ok(manifest):
    """(ok, text): does the manifest's own digest match its content (the runner's check)?"""
    if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
        return False, "not a manifest (not a JSON object)"
    rec = manifest.get("manifest_sha256")
    if not rec:
        return False, "the manifest carries no digest (manifest_sha256)"
    if digest_of(manifest) != rec:
        return False, "the manifest itself was edited after it was written"
    return True, "the manifest digest matches its content"


_ALIASES = {"base": "baseline", "incr": "incremental", "inc": "incremental",
            "increment": "incremental", "vel": "velocity", "arr": "arrival", "hmax": "depth",
            "max": ""}


def _norm_role(s):
    words = str(s or "").lower().replace("_", " ").replace("-", " ").replace("(", " ") \
        .replace(")", " ").split()
    words = [_ALIASES.get(w, w) for w in words]
    words = [w for w in words if w and w != "time"]
    return " ".join(words)


def _entries(manifest):
    out = []
    for group in ("outputs", "inputs"):
        for label, rec in (manifest.get(group) or {}).items():
            if isinstance(rec, dict):
                out.append((group, label, rec))
    return out


def _where(path, dam_folder):
    if path and not os.path.exists(path) and dam_folder:
        alt = os.path.join(dam_folder, os.path.basename(path))
        if os.path.exists(alt):
            return alt
    return path


def compare_rasters(classified, manifest, dam_folder=None):
    """Rows comparing each classified raster {role: path} with the runner's manifest."""
    manifest = manifest or {}
    entries = _entries(manifest)
    rows = []
    for role, path in (classified or {}).items():
        path = str(path or "")
        if path and not os.path.isabs(path) and dam_folder:
            path = os.path.join(dam_folder, path)
        d = file_digest(path) if path else {"missing": True}
        row = {"role": role, "classified_path": path,
               "classified_sha256": d.get("sha256", ""), "manifest_label": "",
               "manifest_path": "", "status": "", "note": ""}
        hit, how = None, ""
        if not d.get("missing"):
            for e in entries:
                rec = e[2]
                if rec.get("sha256") and rec.get("sha256") == d["sha256"] and \
                        (rec.get("size") is None or rec.get("size") == d["size"]):
                    hit, how = e, "digest"
                    break
        name = os.path.basename(path).lower()
        if hit is None and name:
            for e in entries:
                if os.path.basename(str(e[2].get("path", ""))).lower() == name:
                    hit, how = e, "name"
                    break
        if hit is None:
            nr = _norm_role(role)
            for e in entries:
                if nr and _norm_role(e[1]) == nr:
                    hit, how = e, "role"
                    break
        if hit is not None:
            group, label, rec = hit
            row["manifest_label"] = label
            row["manifest_path"] = _where(str(rec.get("path", "")), dam_folder)
        notes = []
        if d.get("missing"):
            row["status"] = "MISSING"
            notes.append("the classified raster is not there any more; nothing to compare")
        elif how == "digest":
            row["status"] = "MATCH"
            notes.append("same digest as the run's '{}'".format(hit[1]))
            if d.get("sampled"):
                notes.append("large file: sampled digest (start, middle, end)")
        elif how in ("name", "role"):
            row["status"] = "DIFFERENT"
            if hit[2].get("missing") or not hit[2].get("sha256"):
                notes.append("the manifest recorded '{}' without a digest".format(hit[1]))
            else:
                notes.append("same {} as the run's '{}' but another digest: the raster was "
                             "replaced or changed after the run".format(
                                 "file name" if how == "name" else "role", hit[1]))
        else:
            row["status"] = "NOT IN MANIFEST"
            notes.append("no raster of the run has this digest, file name or role")
        if hit is not None and hit[0] == "inputs":
            notes.append("found among the run's inputs")
        row["note"] = "; ".join(notes)
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


def chain_summary(rows):
    """Plain-text summary of compare_rasters rows (for a submittal / log)."""
    rows = list(rows or [])
    if not rows:
```
